rows.quantity: D2.3 headline result, stated clean for publication: DKT benchmark, offset sphere pair, D/h=8, frictional vs frictionless contact, both runs one binary lineage (pe f9b7115), decks differing only in the two friction coefficients
rows.expected: full Fortes drafting-kissing-tumbling sequence under both contact models; friction expected to modulate the tumble rate
rows.expectedSource: Fortes, Joseph & Lundgren 1987 (DKT); tilt convention: unfolded 0-180 pair axis (>90 = role exchange)
rows.measured: Both contact models complete the full drafting-kissing-tumbling sequence. Drafting is byte-identical between the two runs (all 720 shared pre-contact samples of tilt and separation, max delta 0.0); kissing at t = 18.10. Frictional (mu_s/mu_d = 0.1/0.05): tilt grows exponentially from contact, doubling every ~3 t.u., 16.2 deg at t = 25. Frictionless: 21.7 deg at t = 25, 67.1 at t = 30, past horizontal by t = 35 (101.6), 107.2 at t = 40 with roles exchanged (trailer now settling faster, vz -0.401 vs -0.337). Friction retards tumble onset by ~25 percent in tilt at matched time and does not suppress the instability; for liquid-immersed particle contacts near-zero friction or a lubricated contact model is the physical choice (practitioner's guide section 6)
